html:
In October 1970 the Front de liberation du Quebec, a separatist group that had set off bombs since 1963, kidnapped the British diplomat James Cross and the Quebec minister Pierre Laporte in Montreal.

Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau invoked the War Measures Act, the only time it was used in peacetime. Troops patrolled Montreal and Ottawa, and police arrested about 500 people, most of whom were never charged. Asked how far he would go, Trudeau said, "Just watch me."

Laporte was found murdered on 17 October. Cross was freed in December in exchange for his kidnappers' safe passage to Cuba. The crisis discredited violence, and Quebec nationalism turned to elections and the Parti Quebecois that grew from the Quiet Revolution. It remains a debated use of power in a Canadian democracy.
sum: In October 1970 the Front de liberation du Quebec, a separatist group that had set off bombs since 1963, kidnapped the British diplomat James Cross and the Quebec minister Pierre Laporte in Montreal.
